introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

Le mur est lisse, le sol rugueux (mu = 1/racine(3)), l'echelle uniforme de longueur 4 m et de poids w.
Q11(ii) : g = 10 m/s^2 (consigne de la page de garde) ; la pente est donnee par sin(theta) = 1/24 et la resistance est supposee constante.

Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks » ; total 66 + 17 + 17 = 100).
Le sujet est une photo numerisee (CamScanner) : texte lu en image page par page ; les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ont ete ignores.

questions.enonce_markdown:
11. (i)

![fig-1](gce-ol-additional-maths-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_11_fig_1.png)

The figure above shows a uniform ladder of length $4\,\text{m}$ and weight $w$ and it is placed with its lower end on a rough horizontal floor and the top end on a smooth vertical wall. Given that the ladder is inclined at an angle $\theta=30^\circ$ to the horizontal floor and the coefficient of friction between the ladder and the floor is $\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$.

Find how far up the ladder a man of weight $2w$ can climb without the ladder slipping off. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let the man stand at a distance $d$ metres from the foot of the ladder, measured along the ladder. The wall is smooth, so it exerts only a horizontal reaction $S$. The floor exerts a normal reaction $R$ (up) and a friction force $F$ (towards the wall, to stop the foot slipping away).

**Vertical forces:** $R=w+2w=3w$.

**Horizontal forces:** $F=S$.

**Limiting friction** (the man is as far up as possible before slipping): $F=\mu R=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}(3w)=\sqrt3\,w$. So $S=\sqrt3\,w$.

**Moments about the foot of the ladder.** The ladder is $4$ m long, so its top is at height $4\sin30^\circ=2$ m. The weight $w$ acts at the middle ($2$ m along the ladder), at horizontal distance $2\cos30^\circ=\sqrt3$ m from the foot; the man's weight $2w$ is at horizontal distance $d\cos30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}d$.

Taking moments about the foot (the normal and friction forces at the foot have no moment):

$$S\times2=w\times\sqrt3+2w\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2}d.$$

Substitute $S=\sqrt3\,w$:

$$2\sqrt3\,w=\sqrt3\,w+\sqrt3\,w\,d\;\Rightarrow\;2=1+d\;\Rightarrow\;d=1.$$

So the man can climb $1$ m along the ladder before it starts to slip (the ladder is $4$ m long, so this is possible).

**Answer: $1$ m up the ladder (measured from the foot).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A car of mass $1200\,\text{kg}$ has power of $6\,\text{kW}$. Given that the maximum speed of the car on a level road is $24\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

a) Calculate the total resistance to the motion of the car at this speed. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Power $=$ driving force $\times$ speed, so $P=Fv$.

At maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the total resistance $R$:

$$R=F=\frac Pv=\frac{6000}{24}=250.$$

**Answer: the total resistance is $250$ N.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Given that the engine is still working at the same rate and that the resistance remains constant, calculate the acceleration of the car up a plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta=\dfrac1{24}$, when the speed of the car is $6\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.

Driving force at $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: $F=\dfrac Pv=\dfrac{6000}{6}=1000$ N.

Forces along the slope (up the slope is positive): driving force $F=1000$, resistance $R=250$ (down the slope), and the component of the weight $mg\sin\theta=1200\times10\times\dfrac1{24}=500$ N (down the slope).

Newton's second law:

$$F-R-mg\sin\theta=ma\;\Rightarrow\;1000-250-500=1200a\;\Rightarrow\;250=1200a.$$

So $a=\dfrac{250}{1200}=\dfrac5{24}\approx0.208$.

**Answer: $a=\dfrac5{24}\approx0.21\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ (up the slope).**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle
